caption: The drawing depicts a rectangular wooden chest with a sloped lid, decorated in a variety of colors including red, green, blue, yellow, and gold. The main body of the chest features a row of seven arched panels, each containing a small, detailed human figure engaged in different actions or poses. The background behind these figures is predominantly red with diamond and floral patterns, and there are green borders and trim outlining the chest and its panels. The top lid is decorated with a repeating diamond and floral motif in red and green. Above the arched panels, there is a narrow band with a floral pattern and a light blue band in the center displaying the painted name "MANUEL GONZALES VARE" in black letters. The lock plate is centrally positioned on the front of the chest, colored in a muted gold or yellow. The ends and sides are similarly ornamented with geometric and floral designs in consistent colors. The background of the entire drawing is plain and off-white, emphasizing the decorative chest as the central object.
title: Chest
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
